html:
The Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs are a union of three peoples who live on and govern the Warm Springs Indian Reservation in central Oregon. The map shows their ancestral lands in 1492, along the Columbia River and the Deschutes River east of the Cascades.

The three peoples are:

  • the Wasco, Chinookan speakers who lived on the Columbia near The Dalles
  • the Warm Springs bands, Sahaptin speakers such as the Tenino, who fished at Celilo Falls
  • the Paiute, a Northern Paiute people from the high desert to the south, moved onto the reservation from 1879

Salmon from the river was the base of life and trade here. Celilo Falls was one of the great fishing and trading places of North America until a dam drowned it in 1957.

The reservation was set up by an 1855 treaty with the United States, under which the Wasco and Warm Springs bands gave up most of their land but kept the right to fish at their usual places.
